name: Spiti & Lahaul
tagline: A cold desert of gompas, fossils and homestays
meta_description: Spiti & Lahaul trip planning: Kaza, Key, Tabo, Chandratal and Keylong, honest bus and homestay costs, road opening months and altitude advice.
summary: Spiti and Lahaul form one high district of Himachal Pradesh behind the Pir Panjal. Spiti is a rain-shadow desert at 3,000–4,500 m with thousand-year-old gompas and fossil villages; Lahaul is greener, reached in two hours from Manali through the Atal Tunnel. Go June to September, by HRTC bus and homestay or by private car.
intro: Spiti means the middle land, the valley between Tibet and India, and it still feels like a place in between. The Spiti river runs from below Kunzum La to its meeting with the Sutlej in Kinnaur, through a cold desert where about 50 mm of rain falls in a year. Villages sit where a side stream makes irrigation possible: green squares of barley and peas around whitewashed houses with flat roofs stacked with firewood and dung cakes. Above them, on ridges, are the gompas that have anchored this valley since the 10th century.

Lahaul is the other half of the district, west of Kunzum La. It gets more snow and more water, so its villages grow potatoes, peas and hops, and willow and poplar line the Chandra and Bhaga rivers. Keylong, the district headquarters, sits at 3,080 m on the Manali–Leh road. Since the Atal Tunnel opened on 3 October 2020, Lahaul has become a two-hour drive from Manali and is reachable for much of the winter.

For travellers this is the most affordable high Himalaya in India. HRTC buses run to Kaza from both Shimla and Manali, shared taxis fill up each morning in season, and a family homestay with dinner and breakfast costs ₹1,200–2,500 a person. There are no five-star hotels, and we say that plainly: the best rooms in Spiti are good, warm, locally built boutique hotels and heated homestay rooms, not resorts.

Altitude is the one thing to plan around. Kaza is at 3,650 m, Key Gompa at 4,166 m, and Langza, Hikkim and Komic sleep at 4,400 m or more. Enter from the Shimla side through Kinnaur if you can, because the gradual climb through Nako and Tabo is the safest acclimatisation on any Himalayan road trip. Coming from Manali, take an easy first day in Kaza and talk to your doctor before you go.

story.title: From a vanished sea to the tunnel road

chapters.heading: Fossils of the Tethys
chapters.text: The scree around Langza and Hikkim is full of ammonites, the coiled shells of sea creatures that lived in the Tethys Ocean before India collided with Asia and pushed the seabed up into mountains. In the 19th century the geologist Ferdinand Stoliczka studied the rock layers near Mud village in Pin Valley and named one of them the Muth succession; the valley is still a field school for Himalayan geology. Villagers call the fossils by their own names and once kept them in household shrines. Today the rule is simple and worth repeating: look, photograph, and leave them where they lie. Removing fossils strips the slopes that make Langza special, and village councils ask visitors not to buy or carry them away.

chapters.heading: The translator's temples
chapters.text: In 996 CE the translator Rinchen Zangpo founded Tabo on behalf of Yeshe-Ö, king of Guge in western Tibet, at a time when the kings were reviving Buddhism after a century of decline. Tabo's mud-walled assembly hall still holds paintings and clay sculptures from its early centuries, which is why it is called the Ajanta of the Himalayas and protected by the Archaeological Survey of India. Nako's temple complex, a day's drive south, is also linked to Rinchen Zangpo. Key Gompa, founded in the 11th century, was attacked by Mongols in the 17th century and damaged again in the wars of the 19th, and each time it was rebuilt by the community it serves.

chapters.heading: Forts on cliffs and the eldest son
chapters.text: Dhankar means fort on a cliff, and for a time in the 17th century it was the capital of Spiti, chosen because a ridge 300 m above the Spiti–Pin confluence was easy to defend. Land was scarce and water scarcer, so Spitian families protected their fields through primogeniture: the eldest son inherited the house and land, and younger sons traditionally joined a monastery. Fraternal polyandry was part of the same logic of keeping farms whole. Both customs have largely faded with schools, roads and jobs, but they explain why almost every family in Spiti has a link to a gompa, and why the big monasteries became the valley's schools, archives and banks.

chapters.heading: Barter fairs to the tunnel road
chapters.text: For centuries Spiti traded across high passes. Traders from Ladakh crossed Parang La, at 5,578 m, to Kibber, and met traders from Rampur-Bushahr and Spiti at the Ladarcha fair to swap wool, salt, grain and dried fruit. The fair now takes place in Kaza each August. In 2002 a group of locals and professionals began working with sea buckthorn, the thorny shrub whose orange berries grow along Spiti's rivers, and the work grew into homestays and solar-heated rooms that now carry much of the valley's tourism. Then in 2020 the Atal Tunnel cut under Rohtang Pass, and Lahaul, once cut off for half the year, became a two-hour drive from Manali.

highlights.title: Tabo, founded in 996 CE
highlights.text: The mud-walled assembly hall at Tabo is more than a thousand years old and still in use. Its paintings and clay sculptures are the reason scholars call it the Ajanta of the Himalayas. Go in daylight, without flash, and give your eyes a minute to adjust to the dark.

highlights.title: Key Gompa above the Spiti river
highlights.text: Key Gompa is stacked on a conical hill at 4,166 m, 12 km from Kaza. It belongs to the Gelug school, trains young monks, and was rebuilt after Mongol raids and the 1975 earthquake. Arrive for morning prayers and you may be offered butter tea.

highlights.title: Fossil slopes of Langza
highlights.text: Langza sits at about 4,400 m under Chau Chau Kang Nilda, with a large Buddha statue facing the valley. The slopes around it hold marine fossils from the Tethys sea. Look and photograph, but leave every fossil where it lies.

highlights.title: Chandratal, a Ramsar wetland
highlights.text: The crescent lake at about 4,250 m was declared a Ramsar wetland in November 2005. Camps sit about 2–3 km away by rule, and the last kilometre is on foot. The road opens roughly mid-June to early October; check current status before you travel.

highlights.title: Pin Valley and its snow leopards
highlights.text: Pin Valley National Park, set up in 1987, covers 675 km² of cold desert south of Spiti. It shelters Siberian ibex, blue sheep and snow leopards. Mudh, the last village on the road, is the base for walks and the start or end of the Pin–Parvati trek.

highlights.title: Lahaul through the Atal Tunnel
highlights.text: The 9.02 km Atal Tunnel cut the drive from Manali to Keylong to about two hours. Beyond it lies Kardang Gompa, where monks and nuns share one monastery, Jispa's riverside camps, and the Manali–Leh road climbing towards Baralacha La.

money_savers: Take the HRTC bus from Manali to Kaza (about ₹400–600) instead of a shared taxi seat (about ₹1,200–1,800); it leaves around 5 am in season.
Women travel at half fare on HRTC buses within Himachal Pradesh, which halves the cost of a bus circuit; check current status before you travel.
Book homestays with dinner and breakfast included (₹1,200–2,500 a person); Kaza cafes charge ₹300–600 for a meal.
Split a Kaza taxi for the Key, Kibber, Langza, Hikkim and Komic loop between four people and it drops to about ₹1,000–1,500 each.
Travel in the first half of June or in September: room prices fall by a quarter to a third compared with July and August.
Fill a steel bottle with filtered water at homestays and cafes in Kaza; it saves money and keeps plastic bottles out of a valley with no landfill.
getting_there: There are two roads in. From Shimla, the Hindustan–Tibet road (NH-5) runs through Kinnaur to Reckong Peo, and NH-505 continues past Nako and Tabo to Kaza: about 420 km, best done in two or three days, and open most of the year apart from landslides and heavy snow. From Manali, the road goes through the Atal Tunnel to Gramphu, then along the rough Chandra valley track past Chhatru and Batal and over Kunzum La to Kaza: about 180–200 km and 9–11 hours, open roughly June to October. Keylong is 71 km from Manali through the tunnel. The nearest airports are Bhuntar (for Manali), Shimla and Chandigarh. Check current status before you travel.
permits: Indian citizens do not need any permit for Spiti or Lahaul. Foreign nationals need a Protected Area Permit for the stretch near the Tibet border between Kinnaur and Spiti, which includes Nako and the road to Sumdo; it is issued at offices such as the SDM in Kaza or Reckong Peo and in Shimla, usually for groups arranged through an agent. Rohtang Pass needs a vehicle permit, but the Atal Tunnel route does not. Rules change, so check current status before you travel.

months.weather: Kaza −18 to −2 °C, dry cold, snow spells
months.summary: Deep winter. The Manali side is shut at Kunzum, so Spiti is reached only from Shimla through Kinnaur, and even that road can close for a day or two after snow. Water pipes freeze, many cafes close, and homestays heat one room with a bukhari stove. This is the month for snow leopard trips from Kibber and for Halda, Lahaul's festival of torches. Only go with warm gear, a flexible return date and a local operator.
months.tip: Pack a down jacket rated for −20 °C and keep phone batteries inside your clothes.

months.summary: Still winter, but the days are clearer and longer. Snow leopard sightings around Kibber and Chicham peak in this window because the cats follow blue sheep down to lower slopes. Kaza's market is quiet and most hotels are closed; heated homestays are the base. The Kinnaur road is usually open but slow over ice. Keylong and Sissu get heavy snow; the Atal Tunnel stays open except in bad weather.
months.tip: Book winter homestays through a Kaza operator who can confirm they have water and heat.

months.summary: The awkward month. Winter wildlife trips wind down, snow can still fall heavily, and the thaw makes the Kinnaur road prone to rockfall. Hotels and cafes in Kaza remain mostly shut, and the Manali side stays closed. We do not run trips in March apart from specialist winter departures, and we suggest waiting for May or June unless you are already experienced with Himalayan winter travel.
months.tip: If you must go, carry chains or travel with a local driver who knows the ice spots.

months.summary: Spring arrives slowly. Fields are ploughed with dzo, apricot trees in lower Kinnaur flower, and Kaza starts to reopen by the end of the month. The Manali–Kaza road over Kunzum is still under snow, so the only way in is from Shimla. Langza and Komic may still have snow on the access road. A quiet month for a Kinnaur and lower Spiti trip, not yet for the full circuit.
months.tip: Plan a Shimla-in, Shimla-out loop in April; do not count on Kunzum La.

months.summary: Kaza is open again, homestays restock, and barley goes into the fields. The Shimla route is the reliable way in. Kunzum La and the Batal stretch are usually cleared by BRO between late May and June, and Chandratal opens later still, so a Manali exit is possible only late in the month in a good year. Check current status before you travel. Prices are low and roads are quiet.
months.tip: Carry sunscreen and lip balm: the UV at 4,000 m in May is harsh.

months.summary: The season opens properly. The Manali–Kaza road and Kunzum La are normally open by mid-June, Chandratal camps set up, and HRTC restarts its Manali–Kaza bus. Spiti barely notices the monsoon, so June to September is reliable here. Lahaul's gompas hold Tsheshu masked dances in June and July. The first half of June is quieter and cheaper than the school-holiday rush.
months.tip: Book Chandratal camps once the road opening is confirmed, not before.

months.weather: Kaza 9 to 24 °C, dry; rain in Kinnaur
months.summary: Peak season. Peas and barley are green, wildflowers cover the meadows near Chandratal, and every village loop is open. Key Gompa holds its Chham masked dance, usually in July; dates are set by the monastery. The catch is the approach roads: monsoon rain in Kinnaur and on the Manali side can trigger landslides that close a road for hours or days. Build in one spare day.
months.tip: Keep a spare day in any July itinerary for landslides on the approach roads.

months.weather: Kaza 9 to 23 °C, dry; heavy rain on approaches
months.summary: Inside Spiti the weather is still fine, and the Ladarcha fair fills the Kaza ground in the third week. Getting in and out is the problem: August is the worst month for landslides at Malling in Kinnaur and for swollen streams between Chhatru and Batal. Trips still run, but slower and with more uncertainty. We rate August good, not best, for that reason.
months.tip: Cross the Chhatru–Batal streams early in the morning, when snowmelt is lowest.

months.summary: Our favourite month. The monsoon has left the approach roads, skies are clean, barley turns gold and harvest starts. Sea buckthorn berries ripen orange along the rivers. Crowds thin after the first week and room prices fall. Nights get cold, close to freezing in Kaza and below it at Chandratal and Langza, so pack layers.
months.tip: September is the best month to taste fresh sea buckthorn juice in Kaza.

months.summary: Autumn colours in Lahaul's willows and poplars, empty roads and the clearest light of the year. Chandratal camps pack up early in the month and Kunzum La can close after the first heavy snow in late October or November, so plan to leave by the Shimla road if you travel late. Many homestays slow down after harvest. Check current status before you travel.
months.tip: From mid-October, plan your exit via Kinnaur in case Kunzum La closes.

months.summary: The season closes. Kunzum La shuts with the first big snow, cafes and most hotels in Kaza close, and families finish storing food for winter. Spiti's own Losar new year is often marked around this time, but it is a family festival rather than an event for visitors. We do not recommend November apart from short Kinnaur trips to Nako.
months.tip: Treat November as off season and keep any trip to the Kinnaur side.

months.summary: Winter settles in. The only road is through Kinnaur, and it can close for days after snowfall. Some winter specialist operators start snow leopard trips late in the month. Lahaul is reachable through the Atal Tunnel, and Sissu sees snow tourism from Manali, but Keylong itself is quiet and very cold. Only go with a winter-experienced local operator.
months.tip: Check whether the Atal Tunnel is open for tourist vehicles on the day you plan to cross.

faqs.q: How much does a Spiti trip cost on a budget?
faqs.a: A Spiti trip by HRTC bus and shared taxi with homestays costs about ₹2,000–3,500 a person a day, so an 8-night circuit comes to roughly ₹22,000–32,000 excluding travel to Shimla or Manali. Homestays with two meals are ₹1,200–2,500, the Manali–Kaza bus is about ₹400–600 and shared taxi seats on the same route are ₹1,200–1,800. Prices are indicative for 2026.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Spiti?
faqs.a: June to September is best. The Manali–Kaza road over Kunzum La is normally open from about mid-June to October, and Spiti sits in a rain shadow, so July and August are dry inside the valley even when the approach roads see landslides. September has the clearest skies. Winter trips from January to February are possible from the Shimla side only. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is altitude sickness a problem in Spiti?
faqs.a: Yes, take it seriously. Kaza is at 3,650 m and villages like Langza, Hikkim and Komic are above 4,400 m. Coming in from Shimla through Nako and Tabo gives a gradual climb; from Manali you jump to Kaza in a day. Rest on day one, drink water, avoid alcohol, climb high and sleep lower. Descend if symptoms worsen, and talk to your doctor about medication before you go.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for Spiti Valley?
faqs.a: Indian citizens do not need a permit for Spiti or Lahaul. Foreign nationals need a Protected Area Permit for the border stretch between Kinnaur and Spiti, which includes Nako and Sumdo, issued in Kaza, Reckong Peo or Shimla, usually for travellers in a group arranged by an agent. The Atal Tunnel route needs no permit. Rules change, so check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Which is better: Spiti from Shimla or from Manali?
faqs.a: Enter from Shimla and leave via Manali if you can. The Kinnaur road climbs slowly through Nako (3,625 m) and Tabo (3,050 m), which helps acclimatisation, and it is open most of the year. The Manali road is shorter but rougher, crosses Kunzum La at about 4,590 m, and is open only from about June to October. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Does mobile network and internet work in Spiti?
faqs.a: Partly. BSNL and Jio work in Kaza, Tabo, Keylong and many villages, and Airtel has improved in Kaza. Speeds drop at night and in bad weather. There is no signal between Losar and Chhatru, including Kunzum La, Batal and Chandratal. Some homestays and cafes in Kaza have Wi-Fi. Tell family when you will be out of range.

faqs.q: Are there ATMs and petrol pumps in Spiti?
faqs.a: Kaza has ATMs and the only petrol pump in Spiti, and Keylong and nearby Tandi serve Lahaul. ATMs can run out of cash in peak season and fail when the network is down, so carry enough cash for several days. UPI works where there is signal, but homestays in Langza or Mudh may prefer cash. Fill the tank in Kaza or Tandi.

faqs.q: Is Spiti safe for solo women travellers?
faqs.a: Spiti is one of the safer regions in India for solo women, and many travel here by HRTC bus and stay in family homestays or Zostel in Kaza. The real risks are road conditions and altitude, not people. Share your plan, avoid driving or walking alone after dark on highway stretches, and choose homestays recommended by your hostel or operator.

faqs.q: Can I take children or senior citizens to Spiti?
faqs.a: Yes, with care. Choose the Shimla approach for a slower climb, sleep in Kaza, Tabo and Nako rather than in villages above 4,000 m, and keep drive days under six hours. Medical facilities are basic, with the main hospital in Kaza and bigger ones in Reckong Peo and Manali. Talk to your doctor before taking young children or anyone with heart or lung conditions.
